summary: Proceed with no companion. This is a cheap, untested extension of the landed w2 atomic flag to the verify shapes. The mechanism is weak, though, and the expected effect sits at the noise floor at bs=256, so make the run self-interpreting: time w2 master vs atomic in prepare() with CUDA events and print it. Also keep the verify mode decision fully separate from the T<=32 one, and make the run report whether the gate picked master, which would make the run a silent no-op.
justification: Plausibility: low to moderate. The hypothesis explains the bs=256 swing by a lock-serialized fp32 reduce. Its evidence is the Marlin pair row moving 391.4 us (FINDINGS best profile, job 1947e3ec) to 451.5 us (a2744bc496b84790 profile) on identical verify code, with timed bs=256 at 454.28 vs 467.80 us. That shows variance, not its cause. Nothing in either profile separates the w2 launch from w13 (one row, calls=2), and nothing measures slice_count. The closest prior evidence points against a reduce bottleneck at verify. w13-marlin-bf16-reduce-verify (use_fp32_reduce=False on w13 at T>=128) was within-ci flat. w13-marlin-atomic-add-small-m was flat. The landed w2 atomic run moved only bs=1 (-3.9 us), and bs=8/16/32 were flat even though they are the shapes with deeper K-slicing than verify. At verify, w2 has more m-blocks (bs=256: about 2048 global routes skewed onto the 32 local experts, block_size_m=32), so with 528 resident CTAs (workspace max_blocks_per_sm=4) and 16-32 n-tiles each, slice_count should be about 1. Atomic add then removes almost no reduce and just turns stores into atomics. A factual error in the change paragraph: block_size_m at bs=128/256 is 16/32, not 8/16. _block_size_m gives 48/64, and the two-smaller pick turns that into 16/32 (bs=257 also 32). Size versus floors: verify_16 is 317.8 us (floor 101.3) and verify_32 is 467.8 us (floor 108.9). Marlin is about 96% of both, so there is headroom, but the claimed -5..-15 us at bs=128 is 1.5-4.7%, and -10..-30 us at bs=256 is 2-6.4%. Identical-code noise at bs=256 is already about 3% (454 vs 468). Only the upper end of the range would be readable per shape, and one load moving 3% moves the geomean about 0.5%, inside the ±1.5% CI. The directions match the shape weights (all 60), and bs<=32 flat is right, because those shapes run master's landed path byte for byte. WEAKEST LINK: the 'swing = lock slow mode' inference. It has no profile or slice_count evidence, and the bs=8-32 flat result plus the w13 verify reduce flat result both suggest the reduce is not where verify time goes. Second weak link: numerics headroom. The landed T<=32 self-check chose atomic with worst rel-L2 vs master 0.00479 against a 5e-3 gate (log a2744bc496b84790 L148). That margin is thin, and at T in {33,128,256,257} with skewed routing the gate may pick 'master', which would make the run flat by construction.
confounders: w2-marlin-atomic-add-small-m (9080a71): same flag, same call, same self-check machinery. Risk 1: if the implementer reuses state['w2_mode'] or makes T<=32 depend on the verify self-check passing, a verify-range failure would turn bs=1 back to master and show up as a bs=1 'regression' that has nothing to do with verify. Keep a separate key (e.g. state['w2_mode_verify']), and leave the T<=32 branch and its self-check untouched. Risk 2: if the verify check picks atomic_zero, cache3.zero_() at bs=256 clears num_tokens*8*4096*2 B = 16.8 MB (8.4 MB at bs=128). That is a ~4-7 us memset, which by itself cancels the low end of the expected gain. Read the memset row.

marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm (cefc282): sets block_size_m 16/32 at verify, which sets the m-block count and therefore slice_count, the only lever atomic add acts on. Under SGLang's 48/64 there would be fewer m-blocks and possibly deeper K-slicing, so a flat result here does not retire the knob for other block_m picks, and a gain does not transfer if block_m is retuned. Fixed on master, so it does not confound this run's sign.

sglang-marlin-path-parity (a646cb4): the shared workspace (max_blocks_per_sm=4 -> 528 CTAs) sets the grid and therefore slice_count for both calls. Fixed on master, so not a confound for this run, but the result only holds for this workspace.

align-parallel-per-expert-verify (1a5da3d): produces sorted_ids/block_experts/n_padded at T>32. The padding rows and the -1 sentinel for remote routes decide which C rows Marlin touches. Under atomic add, remote and padded rows must stay untouched exactly as under plain store, or the SGLang combine (slot_expert_ids masking) reads garbage. The T=33/257/skewed self-check covers this as long as it compares the final combined output, not just y.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m (192f225): no interaction at T>32, which uses SGLang's fused_post_expert_norm_weighted_sum. It matters only that cache3 still aliases cache13 (non-zero stale cache1 data), so that the verify self-check is a true test of whether Marlin's atomic path pre-zeroes C.
interference: No companion is warranted. The ambiguity in a single run is noise at bs=256 plus an unattributed mechanism, and none of ab-revert, ab-tune or control fixes either. Reverting block-m-two-smaller or the small-m atomic patch would only measure a different configuration. A 'use_fp32_reduce=False at w2 verify' control would test a different knob, which is the w2 twin of an already-flat w13 run. The cheaper and stronger fix is in-run: in prepare() (untimed, synthetic inputs only), after the self-check, time the w2 moe_wna16_marlin_gemm call alone with CUDA events at T=128 and T=256. Use the skewed routing, flush L2 with a >50 MB buffer write before each rep, and take the median of ~50 reps each for 'master' and the chosen atomic mode. Print '[w2-atomic-verify] T=128 master X us atomic Y us; T=256 ...'. This gives a paired, same-process A/B of exactly the changed launch. A per-shape gain then counts only if the prepare A/B agrees in sign, and a flat or loss result retires w2 atomic at verify regardless of headline noise. Also print the chosen verify mode and the worst rel-L2 per T. If the verify gate chose master, harvest the run as a no-op, not as 'flat'.
rules_flags: None blocking. Atomic add makes the w2 sum order nondeterministic run to run. TASK.md has no determinism requirement and checks rel-L2 per call (output <=1.5%, any row <=5x, no NaN/Inf), so this is fine, but the self-check must gate on the final kernel_fn output, not on y.
Branch on num_tokens and the prepare-time mode string only. Never derive the mode from data or cache anything from data, and keep the self-check on synthetic seeded inputs (as the landed one does).
cache3.zero_() (if atomic_zero is chosen) is graph-capturable. Make sure no .item()/synchronize from the self-check or the proposed prepare-time timing leaks into kernel_fn's path.

Precision: 5e-3 vs master is an internal gate, not the judge's bound. Do not loosen it silently. If you widen it for verify, also gate on worst per-row rel-L2 (for example <=2% vs master) so a skewed bs=257 row cannot approach the 7.5% per-row limit.
open_questions: Spec fix: block_size_m at bs=128/256/257 is 16/32/32 (SGLang 48/64/64, two candidates down), not 8/16 as the change paragraph says.

What is w2's slice_count at T=128/256 under block_m 16/32 and 528 CTAs? If it is 1, atomic add saves no reduce, and the expected-faster rows have no mechanism. The prepare-time event timing answers this indirectly.

Will the verify gate pass? T<=32 passed at 0.00479 vs 5e-3. Log the worst rel-L2 at each of T=33/128/256/257 with skewed and random routing. If any T fails, decide up front whether to gate per T (allowed: branching on shape) or treat the whole verify range as master.

Does the Marlin MoE launcher zero C itself when use_atomic_add=True (the landed check chose 'atomic' with no memset on a stale aliased buffer, which implies it does or that slice 0 plain-stores)? If it zeroes internally, a ~16.8 MB internal memset at bs=256 may hide inside the Marlin row and eat any gain.

The 391 vs 451 us Marlin-row swing at bs=256 appears in profile rows on identical code. Is it clock or thermal variance? Comparing the SGLang column at bs=256 across the two runs (616.0 vs 629.5 us, also +2%) suggests at least part of it is machine-wide, not a Marlin-specific slow mode.
